findings.statement: TNFa pathway activity is higher at baseline in non-responders to ustekinumab (BH padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000484]) and also in UNIFI placebo non-responders (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.00608]), but not in PURSUIT placebo (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (PURSUIT).padj=0.932]); this marks general severity rather than a drug-specific mechanism.

NFkB activity is associated with non-response in all four biologic arms after correction, for example infliximab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.infliximab.padj=0.000294]), and also in UNIFI placebo, so it behaves as a shared severity axis, not a mechanism of one drug.

JAK-STAT activity is associated with non-response to ustekinumab and infliximab but not to golimumab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.golimumab.padj=0.204]) or vedolizumab (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.vedolizumab.padj=0.571]); the signal is not uniform across drugs.

TGFb pathway activity is higher in ustekinumab non-responders (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.000493]) but not in golimumab non-responders (padj [type=response_pathway; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.golimumab.padj=0.348]); UNIFI placebo is also significant, so severity is a likely confounder.

OSM is higher at baseline in ustekinumab non-responders (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000264]), but the drug-versus-placebo interaction is null (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; interaction.ustekinumab.padj=0.971]) and UNIFI placebo has a similar effect size (padj [gene=OSM; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.116]); no golimumab, infliximab or vedolizumab signal survives correction. Treat as a severity marker, not a drug-specific one.

TREM1 is associated with ustekinumab non-response (padj [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.0000474]) but also separates UNIFI placebo non-responders (padj [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0234]) and the interaction is null (padj [gene=TREM1; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; interaction.ustekinumab.padj=0.983]); this is a severity signal.

CXCL8 (rank 3 in convergence) is higher in ustekinumab non-responders (padj [gene=CXCL8; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.000102]) and in UNIFI placebo non-responders (padj [gene=CXCL8; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0154]); no other biologic arm survives correction.

CXCR2 is the top convergence candidate (six evidence streams, up in five cohorts, tractable with clinical-stage antagonists). Its baseline level is associated with ustekinumab non-response (padj [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=9.69e-6]) but also with UNIFI placebo non-response (padj [gene=CXCR2; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj=0.0126]), so it reflects neutrophil-driven severity and not a ustekinumab-specific mechanism.

IL23A baseline expression is not associated with ustekinumab response (padj [gene=IL23A; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.ustekinumab.padj=0.977]); the drug's own target does not stratify response.

ITGB7 expression is not associated with vedolizumab response (padj [gene=ITGB7; type=treatment_response; source=ANALYSIS:treatment; arms.vedolizumab.padj=0.995]), though the vedolizumab cohort is small.

LAX1 is the strongest first-in-class discovery candidate, but its composition verdict is partly composition and its main source in inflamed mucosa is plasma cells (share [gene=LAX1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; top_clusters_inflamed.0.share=0.433]); the second dataset does not replicate the T/NK lineage call, so the rise likely reflects immune infiltration.

XKR9 is epithelial and classified intrinsic, but it is up in only a minority of cohorts (cohorts up [gene=XKR9; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; cohorts_up=2]) and the lineage is not replicated in the second dataset; replication is the main gap.

SDR16C5 is intrinsic to the epithelium (epithelial share [gene=SDR16C5; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.918]) and the epithelial lineage is replicated in the second dataset, making it the cleanest tissue-change candidate; missing are treatment-response data and functional evidence.

CHRDL2 is a stromal (inflammatory fibroblast) gene (stromal share [gene=CHRDL2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.939]) replicated in the second dataset, but its highest vital-organ RNA is the largest among the top candidates (nTPM [gene=CHRDL2; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; vital_max_ntpm=42.6]), a safety question to resolve.

ADGRG3 is the only top-15 candidate with both antibody and small-molecule tractability, but nearly all its transcripts come from neutrophils (neutrophil share [gene=ADGRG3; type=discovery_profile; source=ANALYSIS:discovery; neutrophil_share=0.906]), so it is a cell-infiltration marker more than a tissue change.

caveats: Response associations are cross-sectional baseline differences, not prediction; golimumab, infliximab and vedolizumab arms are small and mostly do not survive BH correction.
Most genes tested separate UNIFI placebo non-responders, so ustekinumab signals largely reflect severity; drug-by-placebo interactions were not significant for any gene tested.
PURSUIT placebo is small and shows no signal for any pathway.
Discovery candidates have no response data here; single-cell shares compare cell types and depend on dissociation, and the Smillie data lack neutrophils.

Convergence-ranking top genes (CXCR2, CXCR1, CXCL8, CD274, IDO1, MMP1) are mostly neutrophil/inflammation markers; only CXCL8, CXCR2, TREM1, OSM, OSMR and TNF were tested for response, and CXCR1, CD274, IDO1, MMP1 were not tested.
